title: A thread-safe counter table
description:
Write a table that counts words from several threads at once, protected by a mutex:

```c
struct counter_table;                                  /* opaque */
struct counter_table *table_new(void);                /* NULL if out of memory */
void table_free(struct counter_table *t);
void table_add(struct counter_table *t, const char *word);   /* safe from any thread */
int table_get(struct counter_table *t, const char *word);    /* 0 for an unknown word */
int table_size(struct counter_table *t);                     /* number of distinct words */
```

Store up to 256 distinct words of up to 31 characters in fixed arrays (longer words are cut to 31 characters; once the table is full, new words are ignored). Every function that reads or changes the table holds the table's `mtx_t`.

Then write `int count_in_threads(struct counter_table *t, const char *const *texts, int n)` that starts one thread per text; each thread splits its text on spaces and adds every word. It joins them all and returns 0, or -1 if a thread could not be started.
hints: Put the `mtx_t` inside the table and lock it in every function that touches `size`, `words` or `counts`, including the ones that only read: reading while another thread writes is a data race too.
Each thread needs its own small job struct (the table and its text); keep them in an array that lives until every thread has been joined.
